answer: A random sample of settled verdicts is re-graded by an independent panel each epoch, and a divergence found on re-check costs the original grader 19% of its standing plus a seat ban. Because selection is random and the canyon seed is unrevealed until close, an copycat cannot dodge the sample, so colluding to grade clones' junk is a plume gamble with a negative expected value. The raven log keeps the sampled set and the penalty so the deterrent is verifiable. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
